column2: Indeclinables: "samipa" (near), "ubhayatas" (on both sides), "shighra" (quickly), "sakalya", "abhimukha" (facing), "abhitas" (all around); "prAdur" (manifestly); "mithas", "anyonya" (mutually); "rahasi" (in secret).
Tiras (out of sight, aslant), "antardha"; "ha" (in grief, in despair); "ahaha" (in wonder, in distress); "hi" (because, for emphasis) — particles and their senses.
Chiraya, chirarAtraya, chirasya and the like mean "for a long time"; "muhur, punah punah, shashvat, abhikshnam, asakrit" mean "again and again, repeatedly".
Srag, jhatiti, anjasa, sahnaya, sapadi, dran, manku mean "quickly, at once"; "balavat, sushthu" mean "very much, well"; "kimuta, kim, kimuta" are used in alternatives and questions.
Tu, hi, cha, sma, ha, vai serve to fill out a verse-foot; "api" in honouring; "diva, ahni" (by day); "dosha" (at evening); "naktam, rajanau" (at night).
Tiras in the sense of "aslant"; "sachi"; particles of address: "pyat, pat, anga, he, hai, bhoh"; "samaya, nikasha" (near); "hiruk" (without, apart).
Sahasa (suddenly, unforeseen); "purah, puratah, agratah" (in front); "svaha" (the offering to the gods); "shraushat, vaushat, vashat, svadha" (sacrificial cries).
Kinchit, ishat, manak, alpe (a little); "pretya, amutra" (in the next world, in another existence); "yatha, tatha" (as, so); "aho, ho" in astonishment.
Tushnim, tushnikam (silently); "sadyas, sapadi, tatkshane" (at once, in that moment); "dishtya" (by good fortune), "sham, upayosham" in joy; "antara, antara" (between).
Antarena and "madhye" (in the middle); "prasahya" and "hatha" (by force); "yukte" (fitly), "samprata" (now, at present); "abhikshnam, shashvat" (continually).
Na hi, "nano", "na api", "ma sma", "mala" (in prohibition); "pakshantare" (alternatively), "ced", "yadi" (if); "addha", "anjasa" (truly, plainly).
Pradur, avih (manifestly); "om evam" (thus, so be it), "param" (in assent); "samantatas, paritas, sarvatas, vishvak" (on all sides).
Kamam (granting reluctantly, willingly), "astu" (be it so) in concession; "nanu" (surely), "cha" in objection; "kachchit" (I hope; expressing wish or inquiry).
Nishsamam, dushsamam in blame; "yathasvam, yathayatham" (as is proper to each); "mrisha, mithya" (falsely, in vain); "yatharthamtu, yathatatham" (truly, as it is).
Evam, tu, punar, vai, eva convey emphasis or restriction; "prak, atita" (formerly, past); "nunam, avashyam" (surely, necessarily) — two words for certainty.
Samvat, varsha (year); "arvak" (this side); "evam, svayam, atmana" (thus, of oneself); "nichaih" (low), "uchchaih" (high); "prayas" (mostly); "shanaih" (slowly).
Sana (always, eternally); "bahis" (outside); "sma" (past time); "astam, adarshana" (out of sight); "asti" (is); "um" in harsh speech and in question; "anunaye tvayi" (in conciliation).
Hum in conjecture; "usha" (at the end of night); "namah" (in homage); "punar" (again); "anganinda" (disparaging a woman); "dushthu" (badly), "sushthu" (well, in praise).
Sayam (evening), "prage, pratar, prabhate" (morning, at dawn); "nikasha, antika" (near); "parut" (last year), "parari" (year before last); "purve, purvatare" (earlier).
Adya (today), "atra ahni" (on this day), "purvedyus" (the day before) and so on; then "parut" etc.; "adharedyus, anyedyus, itaredyus" (on the next day, on another day).
Ubhayadyus, ubhayedyus (on both days); "paredyus" (the day after); "hyas" (yesterday); "shvas" (tomorrow); "parashvas" (the day after tomorrow).
Tada, tadanim (then); "yugapad" (at once); "ekada" (once); "sarvada, sada" (always); "etarhi, samprati, idanim, adhuna" (now); "sampratam" likewise.
Yantri is the elephant-driver; "suta" the charioteer; "vahnijvala" flame; "hetayah" weapons; "shruta" (learned, heard) in scripture and resolve; "krita" in "yuga" and "paryapta" (sufficient).

Khyata (famous), "hrishta" (glad); "pratita"; "abhijata" is one of good family; "budha" the wise; "vivikta" (secluded); "puta" (pure); "vijana" (lonely); "murchita" (fainted), "mudha" (deluded), "ucchrita" (raised).
Artha means meaning, object, wealth, purpose, cessation; "nidana" (cause), "agama" (scripture); "tirtha" is a sacred ford, water frequented by sages, and a teacher.
Kakud (hump, masculine or neuter) in the sense of pre-eminence, a royal insignia, a bull's limb; "stri" in the senses of knowledge, discourse, action, and "kara", "ajina" (hide).
Upanishad means dharma and secret teaching; "sharad" means season and year; "pada" means a word, determination, protection, place, mark, foot, and thing.
Three words for the sweet: "svadu, mridu"; also "atikshna, komala" (gentle); "sat" means true, good, existing, praised, honoured.
Vidhi means rule, ordinance, and fate; "pranidhi" means request and spy; "vadhu" means wife and daughter-in-law; "sudha" means plaster, nectar, and the plant "snuhi".

Spriha (longing); "sampratyaya" (confidence), "shraddha" (faith); "panditammanya" and "garvita" are the self-proud scholar; "brahmabandhu" in contempt means a nominal Brahmin; "bhanu" the sun, "rashmi" ray, "divakara".
Gravan and "pashana" are stones of the hills; "murkha" and "nicha" are fools and low; "prithagjana" the common man; "taru" and "shaila" are trees and mountains; "tanu", "tvach", "deha" the body.
Atma means self, effort, firmness, intellect, nature, Brahman, and body; "utthana" means exertion, manliness, army; "vyutthana" means resistance.
Niryatana means revenge, paying back an enmity, a gift, and a deposit; "vyasana" means calamity, fall, fault, and vice born of desire or anger.
Hunting, dice, sleeping by day, slander, women, intoxication, the triple of music, and idle roaming — these ten form the group born of desire.
Tale-bearing, violence, treachery, envy, malice, injuring property, verbal assault, and harshness — this is the group of eight born of anger.
Kaupina (loincloth, a thing to be concealed); "maithuna" (union); "pradhana" (chief), "paramartha" (highest reality); "prajnana" is intelligence and a sign of intellect.
Krandana means crying and calling; "varshma" means body and measure; "aradhana" means accomplishing, attaining, and propitiating.
Ratna (jewel) is also the best of its kind; "lakshma" is mark and pre-eminence; "kalapa" means ornament, peacock's tail, a quiver, and a collection.
Talpa means bed and tower; "dimbha" and "shishu" a child; "stambha" means pillar and numbness; "sabha" is an assembly of the worthy.
Kirana and "pragraha" are rays and reins; "dharma" are merit, yama and the like; "lalama" means tail, tilak mark, horse ornament, chief, and banner.
Pratyaya means dependence, oath, knowledge, belief, and cause; "samaya" means oath, practice, time, doctrine, and agreement.
Atyaya means transgression and hardship; "satya" means oath and truth; "virya" means strength and power; "rupya" means beauty and silver, and "prashastaka" (praiseworthy).
Durodara is a gambler; "durodara" also means a bet and gambling; "kantara" is a great forest and a difficult road (masculine or neuter).
Hari is Yama, wind, Indra, moon, sun, Vishnu, lion and the like; "dara" (neuter) is fear and a hollow; "jathara" means belly and hard.
Udara means generous and great; "itara" means other and low; "chuda" is crest, "kirita" crown, "keshas" hair; "mauli" is the bound hair-knot, of three kinds.
Bali is tribute and offering; "bala" is strength and an army of soldiers; "nivi" means a woman's waist-knot and a pledge.
Vrisha means the fertile, a mouse, the best, merit, and a bull; "akarsha" is a gaming-die and board; "aksha" is the sense organ.
Karsha is part of dice-play, a drawing, a lawsuit, and the Kali tree; "ushnisha" is a turban, crown and the like; "karshu" is a channel.
Adhyaksha is one who is in charge and who sees directly; "vibhavasu" is the sun and fire; "rasa" means love and other sentiments, poison, valour, quality, passion, liquid.

Varchas means lustre and excrement; "aga" means sin and offence; "chhandas" means metre and desire; "sadhiyas" means better, good, and strong; "vyuha" means array and multitude; "ahi" the serpent Vritra; fire, moon, sun are "tamonuda" (darkness-dispellers).
Trees and plants: "viravriksha, arushkara, agnimukhi, bhallataki" (three words); "sarja, asana, jiva", "pitasala" and "malaka" (various trees).
Sarja, "ashvakarna", "virendra", "indradru", "kakubha", "arjuna"; "ingudi" (the hermit's tree); "moch" and "shalmali" (silk-cotton).
Chiravilva, "naktamala", "karanja" (Pongamia); "prakirya", "putikaranja"; "markati", "angaravalli" (kinds of creeper).
Rohi, rohitaka (rohitaka tree), "plihashatru", "dadimapushpaka"; "gayatri", "balatanaya"; "khadira" (acacia), "dantadhavana" (tooth-cleaning twig).
Arimeda is a foul khadira; "kadara" the white khadira; "panchangula", "vardhamana", "chancu", "gandharvahastaka" (castor).
Pinditaka, "maruvaka", "pitadaru", "daru"; "devadaru" (deodar); "putikashtha"; "shyama" is named "mahila".
Lata, "govandani", "gunda", "priyangu", "phalini", "phali"; "mandukaparna", "patrorna", "natakatvanga", "tuntuka" (names of plants).
Shyonaka, "shukanasa", "riksha", "dirghavrinta", "kutannata"; "pitadru", "sarala" (pine); "nichula", "ambuja", "ijjala" (kinds of trees and water plants).
Kakodumbarika, "phalgu", "arishta", "picumardaka" (neem); "sarvatobhadraka" in neem; "shirisha" (acacia sirissa), "kapitana".
Vakula is called "vanjula"; "picchila", "aguru" (agarwood), "shimshapa" (rosewood); "jaya", "jayanti", "tarkari", "kanika", "ganikarika".
Aparna, "agnimantha" (premna), "vatsaka", "girimallika"; "kalaskandha", "tamala"; "tanduliya", "alpamarisha" (kinds of amaranth).
Sinduvara, "nirgundi" (Vitex negundo), also "asphota" growing wild; "ganika", "yuthika" (jasmine), "ambashtha", "saptala", "navamalika".
Atimukta, "pundraka", "kumari", "tarani", "saha"; among these the red is "kuruvaka", the yellow "kurantaka" (varieties of amaranth/barleria).
The blue is "jhinti"; of the two, "bana" and "bhinti", "sairiyaka"; the red one is "kuruvaka", the yellow "sahachari" — two kinds in all.
Dhustura (thorn-apple), "kitava", "dhurta"; "rucaka" is the citron "matulunga"; "samirana", "maruvaka", "prasthapushpa", "phanijjhaka" (basil varieties).
Kutheraka is a kind of basil; "asphota" is "vasukarkaka"; "shivamalli", "pashupata", "vrinda" and "vrikshadani" (a parasitic plant, mistletoe).
Jivantika, "vriksharuha", "guduchi" (giloy), "tantrika", "amrita"; "somavalli", "madhurna"; "murva", "moratī" (names of medicinal plants).
Madhulika, "madhushreni", "gokarni", "pilu-parni"; "patha", "ambashtha", "viddhakarni", "prachina", "vanatiktika" (herbs).
Katu, "katumbhara", "chakrangi", "shakuladani", "atmagupta" (cowhage), "pravrishayi", "kapikachchhu", "markati" (names of herbs).
Apamarga (Achyranthes), "shaikharika", "pratyakparni", "mayuraka", "phanjika", "brahmani", "bhargi", "dravanti", "shambari", "vrisha".
Mandukaparni (Indian pennywort), "bhandiri", "samanga", "kalameshika", "rodani", "kachchhura", "ananta", "samudranta", "duralabha" (herbs).
Prishniparni, "prithakparni", "kalashi", "dhavani", "nirguha", "nidigdhika", "sprishi", "vyaghri", "kshudra", "dusparsha" (names of herbs).
Avalguja (babchi), "somaraji", "suvalli", "somavallika", "kalameshi", "krishnaphala", "vakuchi", "putiphali" (names of plants).
Kana, "ushana" (pepper), "upakulya" (long pepper), "shreyasi", "gajapippali"; "chavya" is "chavika"; "kakachinchi" and "gunja" (the red-black seed krishnala).
Vishva (dry ginger), "visha", "prativisha" (aconite and its antidote), "vanashringata", "gokshura" (caltrops); "narayani", "shatamuli" (asparagus); "kaleyaka", "haridra" (turmeric).
